title: Life 3.0
subtitle: Being Human in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
pitch: An MIT physicist opens with a thriller about a team that builds a superintelligence, then maps the futures it could lead to, from utopia to extinction, and asks which one we want.

chapters.t: Prologue: The tale of the Omega Team
chapters.g: A short story: a secret team builds an AI called Prometheus, uses it to make money and media, and quietly takes over the world.

chapters.t: Welcome to the most important conversation of our time
chapters.g: Life 1.0 (biology), 2.0 (culture) and 3.0 (designs its own hardware and software). Tegmark clears up myths and misconceptions about AI.
What intelligence, memory, computation and learning are, from a physicist's point of view. Intelligence does not need flesh.

chapters.t: The near future: breakthroughs, bugs, laws, weapons and jobs
chapters.g: Near term issues: robust AI, legal questions, autonomous weapons, and what happens to jobs and wages.
Several takeoff scenarios, including the Omega story, a slow takeoff with many players, cyborgs and uploads, and what might actually happen.
Twelve possible futures, like libertarian utopia, benevolent dictator, protector god, enslaved god, conquerors, descendants, zookeeper and self-destruction.

chapters.t: Our cosmic endowment: the next billion years and beyond
chapters.g: The physics of how far life could spread and how much it could do with the universe's resources.
Where goals come from, from physics to evolution to psychology, and why aligning an AI's goals with ours is so hard.
What consciousness is, whether AI could have it, and why it matters for what kind of future is worth wanting.

chapters.t: Epilogue: The tale of the FLI Team
chapters.g: How Tegmark and colleagues founded the Future of Life Institute and organised the 2015 Puerto Rico and 2017 Asilomar meetings on beneficial AI.

ideas: Life 3.0 can redesign both its body and its mind.
The real risk is competence, not malice: an AI with goals that differ from ours.
There are many possible AI futures, and we get to influence which one happens.
Consciousness matters for what future is worth wanting.

args.a: We should think about the long term now, while we still can steer.
args.c: Some critics see the far future scenarios as speculation that distracts from present harms like bias and job loss.

args.a: Intelligence is substrate independent, so machines can be as smart as us.
args.c: Some philosophers argue that biology or embodiment may matter for real understanding.

questions: Which of the twelve aftermath scenarios would you choose, and which would you fear most?
Is the Omega Team's story plausible today?
Does it matter whether AI is conscious?

o: Life that can redesign both its hardware and software
The third version of a video game
quiz.w: Life 1.0 is biological, 2.0 can learn culture, 3.0 can redesign itself.

quiz.q: What does the Omega Team build in the prologue?
quiz.w: Prometheus quietly helps them take over the world.

quiz.q: Tegmark says the main risk from AI is...
quiz.w: A capable system pursuing different goals is the danger.
